entries.name: Ackee
entries.use_for: Self-hosted, privacy-focused web analytics with a GraphQL API
entries.why: Lightweight, cookie-free Node analytics; simple to run alongside a site.

entries.name: Analytics (getanalytics.io)
entries.use_for: Send events to multiple analytics providers through one small client API.
entries.why: Provider-agnostic plugin layer so you can swap GA, Segment and others without rewriting tracking code.

entries.name: Aptabase
entries.use_for: Privacy-first analytics for mobile, desktop and web apps
entries.why: Fills the gap for app (not website) analytics, with SDKs for Tauri, Electron, Flutter and Swift.

entries.name: GoAccess
entries.use_for: Analyze web server logs in real time in the terminal or as an HTML report.
entries.why: No tracking script needed; works straight from Nginx/Apache logs.

entries.name: GrowthBook
entries.use_for: Feature flags and A/B testing with warehouse-native experiment analysis
entries.why: Most popular open experimentation platform; SDKs for every stack, MIT core.

license_verified.note: Open-core: MIT except enterprise directories under GrowthBook Enterprise License

entries.name: Jitsu
entries.use_for: Collect events and stream them to your data warehouse, Segment-style
entries.why: Open MIT-licensed Segment alternative for event ingestion into ClickHouse, BigQuery and more.

entries.name: Matomo
entries.use_for: Self-host full-featured web analytics comparable to Google Analytics.
entries.why: The most complete open analytics platform with goals, funnels, heatmaps and full data ownership.

entries.name: OpenPanel
entries.use_for: Open-source Mixpanel alternative: events, funnels, retention and web analytics
entries.why: Combines product and web analytics in one self-hostable AGPL stack with a clean SDK.

entries.name: OpenReplay
entries.use_for: Self-hosted session replay with devtools, product analytics and co-browsing
entries.why: The leading self-hostable session-replay suite; open-core with an AGPL core.

license_verified.note: Open-core: AGPLv3 by default, some dirs MIT, ee/ directory under separate enterprise license

entries.name: OpenSEO
entries.use_for: Self-hosted SEO toolkit for keyword research, rank tracking, backlinks and site audits, with an MCP server for agents.
entries.why: Open-source, pay-as-you-go alternative to Semrush and Ahrefs; self-hostable on Cloudflare or Docker.

entries.name: Plausible Analytics
entries.use_for: Add lightweight, cookie-free website analytics as a Google Analytics alternative.
entries.why: Tiny script, GDPR-friendly, clean dashboard; self-host (AGPL) or use the hosted service.

entries.name: PostHog
entries.use_for: Add product analytics, session replay, feature flags and A/B tests to your app.
entries.why: All-in-one product suite with SDKs for most platforms; self-hostable, MIT core and generous cloud tier.

entries.name: rrweb
entries.use_for: Record and replay user sessions in the browser
entries.why: The session-replay engine behind PostHog and many other replay tools.

entries.name: Rybbit
entries.use_for: Self-host privacy-friendly web and product analytics with funnels and session replay.
entries.why: Fast-growing open alternative that covers both web and product analytics in one tool.

entries.name: Swetrix
entries.use_for: Self-host cookieless web analytics with performance monitoring and error tracking.
entries.why: Privacy-first analytics that adds page speed and error data alongside traffic.

entries.name: Tianji
entries.use_for: Self-host website analytics combined with uptime and server monitoring.
entries.why: One lightweight app for analytics, uptime checks and server status.

entries.name: Umami
entries.use_for: Self-host privacy-friendly website analytics without cookies.
entries.why: MIT licensed, simple to deploy on Postgres and a lightweight tracking script.
